text: The authors discuss the problem of accidents in machine learning systems, defined as unintended and harmful behavior that may emerge from poor design of real-world AI systems, and present five practical research problems. They categorize them by origin: a wrong objective function (avoiding side effects, avoiding reward hacking), an objective function too expensive to evaluate frequently ('scalable supervision'), or undesirable behavior during learning (safe exploration, distributional shift).
title: Five concrete accident-risk problems in AI safety, including scalable oversight
